stemMd: A retailer believes that stockouts of a low-profit replacement part cause customers to abandon purchases of a high-profit main product. It proposes increasing part inventory. Which fact most supports this proposal?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The part is smaller than the main product.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Customer records show that many abandoned main-product purchases are completed when the missing part becomes available.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The part’s own margin is low.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Some customers buy only replacement parts.

explanationMd: The records connect part availability to completion of the profitable complementary purchase. That supports evaluating inventory by its wider contribution rather than its own margin alone.

distractorRationale.a: Physical size does not establish complementary purchasing behaviour.
distractorRationale.c: This is already acknowledged and does not establish indirect value.
distractorRationale.e: Standalone demand does not support the proposed main-product effect.
distractorRationale.d: Brand range alone does not address the stockout mechanism.
